title.zh: 卷89 酷吏:于洛侯 胡泥 李洪之 高遵張赦提 羊祉 崔暹 郦道元
title.en: Volume 89: Cruel Officals: Yu Luohou, Hu Ni, Li Hongzhi, Gaozun Zhang Sheti, Yang Zhi, Cui Xian, Li Dao Yun
title.raw: 卷89 酷吏:于洛侯 胡泥 李洪之 高遵張赦提 羊祉 崔暹 郦道元 Volume 89: Cruel Officals: Yu Luohou, Hu Ni, Li Hongzhi, Gaozun Zhang Sheti, Yang Zhi, Cui Xian, Li Dao Yun

sentences.zh: 于洛侯 胡泥 李洪之 高遵 張赦提 羊祉 崔暹 酈道元 谷楷

translations.literal: Yu Luohou, Hu Ni, Li Hongzhi, Gao Zun, Zhang Sheti, Yang Zhi, Cui Xian, Li Daoyuan, Gu Kai
translations.idiomatic: Yu Luohou, Hu Ni, Li Hongzhi, Gao Zun, Zhang Sheti, Yang Zhi, Cui Xian, Li Daoyuan, and Gu Kai

sentences.zh: 淳風既喪，姦黠萌生；

translations.literal: When pure customs were already lost, treachery and cunning sprang up;
translations.idiomatic: Once honest ways had decayed, deceit and guile began to flourish;

sentences.zh: 法令滋章，刑禁多設。

translations.literal: Laws and statutes grew ever more numerous, and penal prohibitions were set up in abundance.
translations.idiomatic: Statutes multiplied, and criminal restrictions proliferated.

sentences.zh: 為吏罕仁恕之誠，當官以威猛為濟。

translations.literal: As officials, few showed genuine humanity and forbearance; in office they relied on ferocity and severity as their means.
translations.idiomatic: Few magistrates possessed true benevolence and leniency; those in power typically used harsh severity as their tool.

sentences.zh: 魏氏以戎馬定王業，武功平海內，治任刑罰，肅厲為本，猛酷之倫，所以列之今史。

translations.literal: The Wei house established its royal enterprise by arms, pacified the realm within the seas by martial achievement, governed through punishment and penal law, took stern severity as its foundation, and therefore such men of fierce cruelty are recorded in the present history.
translations.idiomatic: The Wei dynasty founded its kingship on horseback, subdued the empire by force of arms, and ruled through punishment—stern severity was its foundation. It is for this reason that these men of brutal cruelty are set down in the present annals.

sentences.zh: 于洛侯，代人也。

translations.literal: Yu Luohou was a man of Dai.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Luohou was a native of Dai.

sentences.zh: 以勞舊為秦州刺史，而貪酷安忍。

translations.literal: Because of meritorious service in the old days he was made Governor of Qinzhou, yet he was greedy, cruel, and calmly ruthless.
translations.idiomatic: On account of long-standing merit he was appointed Governor of Qinzhou, but he was greedy, brutal, and pitiless.

sentences.zh: 州人富熾奪民呂勝脛纏一具，洛侯輒鞭富熾一百，截其右腕。

translations.literal: A man of the province named Fu Chi seized from a commoner, Lü Sheng, one pair of leg wrappings. Luohou immediately had Fu Chi flogged one hundred strokes and cut off his right wrist.
translations.idiomatic: When a local man named Fu Chi seized a pair of leg wrappings from the commoner Lü Sheng, Luohou had him flogged one hundred times on the spot and cut off his right wrist.

sentences.zh: 百姓王隴客刺殺民王羌奴、王愈二人，依律罪死而已，洛侯生拔隴客舌，刺其本，并刺胸腹二十餘瘡。

translations.literal: The commoner Wang Longke had stabbed and killed two men, Wang Qiangnu and Wang Yu; by law he deserved death and nothing more. Luohou pulled out Longke's tongue while he was alive, stabbed his perineum, and stabbed his chest and belly more than twenty times.
translations.idiomatic: The commoner Wang Longke had killed Wang Qiangnu and Wang Yu—an offense that by law merited execution and nothing more. Luohou tore out Longke's tongue while he still lived, stabbed his groin, and drove more than twenty wounds into his chest and belly.

sentences.zh: 隴客不堪苦痛，隨刀戰動。

translations.literal: Longke could not endure the pain; he quivered with each stab of the blade.
translations.idiomatic: Longke could not bear the agony; his body convulsed with every thrust of the knife.

sentences.zh: 乃立四柱磔其手足，命將絕，始斬其首，支解四體，分懸道路。

translations.literal: Then he erected four posts and spiked Longke's hands and feet to them. Only when life was nearly gone did he cut off his head, dismember the four limbs, and hang the pieces along the roads.
translations.idiomatic: He then set up four posts and impaled Longke's limbs upon them. Only when life was nearly extinguished did he behead him, quarter the body, and hang the pieces along the roads.

sentences.zh: 見之者無不傷楚，闔州驚震，人懷怨憤。

translations.literal: Those who saw it were all stricken with pity; the whole province was shaken, and the people nursed resentment and rage.
translations.idiomatic: All who witnessed it were overcome with grief; the entire province was shaken, and the people seethed with resentment.

sentences.zh: 百姓王元壽等一時反叛。

translations.literal: The commoners Wang Yuanshou and others rebelled all at once.
translations.idiomatic: The commoners Wang Yuanshou and others rose in revolt together.

sentences.zh: 有司糾劾。

translations.literal: The responsible offices impeached him.
translations.idiomatic: The authorities impeached him.

sentences.zh: 高祖詔使者於州刑人處宣告兵民，然後斬洛侯以謝百姓。

translations.literal: Emperor Gaozu ordered an envoy to proclaim the matter to soldiers and people at the place of punishment in the province, then executed Luohou to appease the populace.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gaozu sent an envoy to announce the case to soldiers and civilians at the site of execution in the province, then had Luohou beheaded to answer the people's grievances.

sentences.zh: 胡泥，代人也。

translations.literal: Hu Ni was a man of Dai.
translations.idiomatic: Hu Ni was a native of Dai.

sentences.zh: 歷官至司衞監，賜爵永城侯。

translations.literal: He rose through offices to Supervisor of the Palace Guards and was granted the title Marquis of Yongcheng.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through the ranks to Supervisor of the Palace Guards and was ennobled as Marquis of Yongcheng.

sentences.zh: 泥率勒禁中，不憚豪貴。

translations.literal: Ni led and disciplined those within the forbidden precincts and did not fear the powerful and noble.
translations.idiomatic: Ni enforced discipline within the palace and showed no fear of the powerful and privileged.

sentences.zh: 殿中尚書叔孫侯頭應內直而闕於一時，泥以法繩之。

translations.literal: The Palace Attendant Shusun Hutou was on duty for inner attendance but was absent for a time; Ni bound him by law.
translations.idiomatic: When Palace Attendant Shusun Hutou failed to report for his shift on inner palace duty, Ni prosecuted him according to the law.

sentences.zh: 侯頭恃寵，遂與口諍。

translations.literal: Hutou relied on imperial favor and thereupon argued with him face to face.
translations.idiomatic: Hutou, trusting in imperial favor, quarreled with him openly.

sentences.zh: 高祖聞而嘉焉，賜泥衣服一襲。

translations.literal: When Emperor Gaozu heard of it he commended him and bestowed on Ni one suit of clothing.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gaozu heard of this and praised him, granting Ni a suit of robes.

sentences.zh: 出為幽州刺史，假范陽公。

translations.literal: He went out as Governor of Youzhou, with the provisional title Duke of Fanyang.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Governor of Youzhou and given the provisional title Duke of Fanyang.

sentences.zh: 以北平陽尼碩學，遂表薦之。

translations.literal: Because Yang Ni of Beiping was a profound scholar, he submitted a memorial recommending him.
translations.idiomatic: Recognizing Yang Ni of Beiping as a distinguished scholar, he memorialized the throne recommending him for office.

sentences.zh: 遷平東將軍、定州刺史。

translations.literal: He was transferred to General Who Pacifies the East and Governor of Dingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to General Who Pacifies the East and Governor of Dingzhou.

sentences.zh: 以暴虐，刑罰酷濫，受納貨賄，徵還戮之。

translations.literal: Because of his violence and cruelty, his excessive and wanton punishments, and his acceptance of bribes, he was summoned back and executed.
translations.idiomatic: For his brutality, his excessive and arbitrary punishments, and his acceptance of bribes, he was recalled to the capital and put to death.

sentences.zh: 將就法也，高祖臨太華殿引見，遣侍臣宣詔責之，遂就家賜自盡。

translations.literal: When he was about to face the law, Emperor Gaozu received him in audience at Taihua Hall, sent a attendant to proclaim an edict rebuking him, and then granted him suicide at his home.
translations.idiomatic: As he was about to face punishment, Emperor Gaozu received him at Taihua Hall, sent an attendant to read out an edict of rebuke, and then permitted him to take his own life at home.

sentences.zh: 李洪之，本名文通，恒農人。

translations.literal: Li Hongzhi, whose original name was Wentong, was a man of Hengnong.
translations.idiomatic: Li Hongzhi, born Li Wentong, was a native of Hengnong.

sentences.zh: 少為沙門，晚乃還俗。

translations.literal: In youth he was a Buddhist monk; only later did he return to lay life.
translations.idiomatic: In his youth he was a Buddhist monk; he did not return to secular life until later years.

sentences.zh: 真君中，為狄道護軍，賜爵安陽男。

translations.literal: In the Zhenjun era he served as Protector of the Army at Didao and was granted the title Baron of Anyang.
translations.idiomatic: During the Zhenjun reign he served as Protector of the Army at Didao and was ennobled as Baron of Anyang.

sentences.zh: 會永昌王仁隨世祖南征，得元后姊妹二人。

translations.literal: It happened that Prince of Yongchang Ren accompanied Emperor Shizu on the southern campaign and obtained two sisters of the future Empress Yuan.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince Ren of Yongchang accompanied Emperor Shizu on the southern campaign, he captured two sisters of the woman who would become Empress Yuan.

sentences.zh: 洪之以宗人潛相餉遺，結為兄弟，遂便如親。

translations.literal: Hongzhi, as a clansman, secretly sent them gifts; they formed a bond as brothers and thereafter treated one another as kin.
translations.idiomatic: Hongzhi, claiming kinship, secretly sent them gifts; they swore brotherhood and thereafter treated one another as family.

sentences.zh: 頗得元后在南兄弟名字，乃改名洪之。

translations.literal: He learned rather fully the names of the Empress Yuan's brothers in the south and thereupon changed his name to Hongzhi.
translations.idiomatic: Having learned the names of Empress Yuan's brothers in the south, he changed his own name to Hongzhi.

sentences.zh: 及仁坐事誅，元后入宮，得幸於高宗，生顯祖。

translations.literal: When Ren was executed for his offense, the Empress Yuan entered the palace, won favor from Emperor Gaozong, and bore Emperor Xianzu.
translations.idiomatic: When Ren was executed for his crimes, Empress Yuan entered the palace, won the favor of Emperor Gaozong, and bore Emperor Xianzu.

sentences.zh: 元后臨崩，昭太后問其親，因言洪之為兄。

translations.literal: As the Empress Yuan lay dying, Empress Dowager Zhao asked about her kin, and she said that Hongzhi was her brother.
translations.idiomatic: On her deathbed Empress Yuan told Empress Dowager Zhao, when asked about her relatives, that Hongzhi was her brother.

sentences.zh: 與相訣經日，具條列南方諸兄珍之等，手以付洪之。

translations.literal: They took leave of one another for days; she fully listed her brothers in the south, Zhenzhi and the others, and handed the list to Hongzhi in her own hand.
translations.idiomatic: They bade farewell over several days; she wrote out a full list of her brothers in the south, including Zhenzhi, and handed it to Hongzhi in her own writing.

sentences.zh: 遂號為顯祖親舅。

translations.literal: He was thereafter styled the maternal uncle of Emperor Xianzu.
translations.idiomatic: He was thereafter known as Emperor Xianzu's maternal uncle.

sentences.zh: 太安中，珍之等兄弟至都，與洪之相見，敍元后平生故事，計長幼為昆季。

translations.literal: In the Tai'an era, Zhenzhi and his brothers arrived at the capital, met Hongzhi, recounted the Empress Yuan's life story, and reckoned seniority to establish themselves as brothers.
translations.idiomatic: During the Tai'an era, Zhenzhi and his brothers came to the capital, met Hongzhi, recounted the life of Empress Yuan, and arranged themselves as brothers according to age.

sentences.zh: 以外戚為河內太守，進爵任城侯，威儀一同刺史。

translations.literal: As a maternal kinsman of the emperor he was made Administrator of Henei, advanced to Marquis of Rencheng, with pomp equal to that of a provincial governor.
translations.idiomatic: As imperial kin by marriage he was appointed Administrator of Henei and promoted to Marquis of Rencheng, with ceremonial display equal to that of a provincial governor.

sentences.zh: 河內北連上黨，南接武牢，地險人悍，數為劫害，長吏不能禁。

translations.literal: Henei bordered Shangdang to the north and Wulao to the south; the terrain was rugged and the people fierce. Banditry occurred repeatedly, and the chief officials could not suppress it.
translations.idiomatic: Henei lay between Shangdang to the north and Wulao to the south—a rugged region of fierce inhabitants where robbery was frequent and local officials could not suppress it.

sentences.zh: 洪之至郡，嚴設科防，募斬賊者便加重賞，勸農務本，盜賊止息。

translations.literal: When Hongzhi reached the commandery he strictly set up regulations and defenses, offered heavy rewards to those who beheaded bandits, and urged agriculture and fundamental industry; banditry ceased.
translations.idiomatic: Upon reaching the commandery, Hongzhi imposed strict regulations, offered generous bounties for the heads of bandits, and promoted agriculture; banditry came to an end.

sentences.zh: 誅鋤姦黨，過為酷虐。

translations.literal: In rooting out villainous factions he went beyond bounds into cruelty.
translations.idiomatic: In exterminating criminal factions he exceeded all bounds of cruelty.

sentences.zh: 後為懷州刺史，封汲郡公，徵拜內都大官。

translations.literal: Later he became Governor of Huaizhou, was enfeoffed as Duke of Jijun, and was summoned to the post of Grand Director of the Inner Court.
translations.idiomatic: He later served as Governor of Huaizhou, was enfeoffed as Duke of Jijun, and was appointed Grand Director of the Inner Court.

sentences.zh: 河西羌胡領部落反叛，顯祖親征，命洪之與侍中、東郡王陸定總統諸軍。

translations.literal: The Qiang and Hu of Hexi led their tribes in rebellion. Emperor Xianzu campaigned in person and ordered Hongzhi and the Attendant-in-Ordinary, Prince of Dongjun Lu Ding, to command all the armies jointly.
translations.idiomatic: When the Qiang and Hu of Hexi rebelled with their tribes, Emperor Xianzu led the campaign in person and appointed Hongzhi and Attendant-in-Ordinary Lu Ding, Prince of Dongjun, to command all forces jointly.

sentences.zh: 輿駕至并州，詔洪之為河西都將討山胡。

translations.literal: When the imperial carriage reached Bingzhou, an edict appointed Hongzhi General of Hexi to campaign against the Mountain Hu.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor reached Bingzhou, he appointed Hongzhi General of Hexi to subdue the Mountain Hu.

sentences.zh: 皆保險拒戰。

translations.literal: They all held the defiles and resisted in battle.
translations.idiomatic: They all held the mountain passes and resisted.

sentences.zh: 洪之築壘於石樓南白鷄原以對之。

translations.literal: Hongzhi built fortifications on Baiji Plain south of Shilou to confront them.
translations.idiomatic: Hongzhi built fortifications on Baiji Plain south of Shilou to face them.

sentences.zh: 諸將悉欲進攻，洪之乃開以大信，聽其復業，胡人遂降。

translations.literal: The generals all wished to attack, but Hongzhi instead extended great trust, allowed them to resume their livelihoods, and the Hu thereupon submitted.
translations.idiomatic: Though the other generals all favored attack, Hongzhi offered generous terms, permitted them to resume their occupations, and the Hu submitted.

sentences.zh: 顯祖嘉之，遷拜尚書外都大官。

translations.literal: Emperor Xianzu commended him and transferred him to Grand Director of the Outer Court in the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xianzu praised him and promoted him to Grand Director of the Outer Court in the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 後為使持節、安南將軍、秦益二州刺史。

translations.literal: Later he served as Bearer of the Staff of Authority, General Who Pacifies the South, and Governor of the two provinces Qin and Yi.
translations.idiomatic: He later served as Bearer of the Staff of Authority, General Who Pacifies the South, and Governor of Qin and Yi provinces.

sentences.zh: 至治，設禁姦之制，有帶刃行者，罪與劫同，輕重品格，各有條章。

translations.literal: Upon taking office he established regulations against villainy: anyone who went about bearing a blade was guilty of the same crime as robbery; grades of severity and rank each had their articles.
translations.idiomatic: Upon taking office he instituted anti-crime regulations: anyone found carrying a weapon in public was treated as guilty of robbery, with graded penalties set forth in detailed statutes.

sentences.zh: 於是大饗州中豪傑長老，示之法制。

translations.literal: Thereupon he gave a great feast to the eminent men and elders of the province and displayed the laws and regulations to them.
translations.idiomatic: He then held a great banquet for the leading men and elders of the province and presented the new regulations to them.

sentences.zh: 乃夜密遣騎分部覆諸要路，有犯禁者，輒捉送州，宣告斬決。

translations.literal: Then by night he secretly sent horsemen in detachments to patrol all the key roads; whoever violated the prohibitions was seized and sent to the province, publicly announced, and beheaded.
translations.idiomatic: That night he secretly dispatched cavalry to patrol all key roads; violators were seized, brought to the provincial capital, publicly announced, and beheaded.

sentences.zh: 其中枉見殺害者百數。

translations.literal: Among them, those wrongly killed numbered in the hundreds.
translations.idiomatic: Among them, more than a hundred were wrongly executed.

sentences.zh: 赤葩渴郎羌深居山谷，雖相羈縻，王人罕到。

translations.literal: The Chipo Kelang Qiang dwelt deep in the valleys; though nominally under restraint, royal agents rarely reached them.
translations.idiomatic: The Chipo Kelang Qiang lived deep in the mountains; though nominally under imperial control, government agents rarely reached them.

sentences.zh: 洪之芟山為道，廣十餘步，示以軍行之勢，乃興軍臨其境。

translations.literal: Hongzhi cut through the mountains to make a road more than ten paces wide, displayed the momentum of a marching army, and then raised troops to enter their territory.
translations.idiomatic: Hongzhi cut a road through the mountains more than ten paces wide to demonstrate military might, then marched his army into their territory.

sentences.zh: 山人驚駭。

translations.literal: The mountain people were startled and terrified.
translations.idiomatic: The mountain people were astonished and afraid.

sentences.zh: 洪之將數十騎至其里閭，撫其妻子，問所疾苦，因資遺之。

translations.literal: Hongzhi led several dozen horsemen to their villages, comforted their wives and children, asked what hardships they suffered, and bestowed gifts upon them.
translations.idiomatic: Hongzhi rode with several dozen horsemen to their villages, comforted their wives and children, inquired after their hardships, and distributed gifts.

sentences.zh: 眾羌喜悅，求編課調，所入十倍於常。

translations.literal: The Qiang masses were delighted and requested to be registered for taxation; the revenue came to ten times the usual amount.
translations.idiomatic: The Qiang were delighted and volunteered to register for taxation; revenue increased tenfold.

sentences.zh: 洪之善御戎夷，頗有威惠，而刻害之聲聞於朝野。

translations.literal: Hongzhi was skilled in governing the barbarians of the frontier and possessed considerable authority and kindness, yet reports of his cruelty were heard in court and countryside alike.
translations.idiomatic: Hongzhi was skilled at governing frontier peoples and combined authority with kindness, yet his reputation for cruelty was known throughout court and countryside.

sentences.zh: 初，洪之微時，妻張氏助洪之經營資產，自貧至貴，多所補益，有男女幾十人。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Hongzhi was still obscure, his wife Lady Zhang helped Hongzhi manage their property; from poverty to wealth she contributed much, and they had several dozen sons and daughters.
translations.idiomatic: In his early days, when Hongzhi was still obscure, his wife Lady Zhang helped him build their fortune; from poverty to wealth she contributed greatly, and they had several dozen children.

sentences.zh: 洪之後得劉氏，劉芳從妹。

translations.literal: Later Hongzhi took Lady Liu, a cousin of Liu Fang.
translations.idiomatic: Later Hongzhi took Lady Liu, a cousin of Liu Fang, as his wife.

sentences.zh: 洪之欽重，而疏薄張氏，為兩宅別居，偏厚劉室。

translations.literal: Hongzhi held her in high esteem but treated Lady Zhang coldly; he set up two separate households and favored the Liu household.
translations.idiomatic: Hongzhi favored Lady Liu but neglected Lady Zhang; he established two separate households and lavished preference on the Liu family.

sentences.zh: 由是二妻妬競，互相訟詛，兩宅母子，往來如讎。

translations.literal: Hence the two wives competed in jealousy, reviled one another in lawsuits, and the mothers and children of the two households dealt with one another like enemies.
translations.idiomatic: The two wives therefore competed in jealousy, sued and cursed one another, and the mothers and children of the two households treated one another as enemies.

sentences.zh: 及莅西州，以劉自隨。

translations.literal: When he took up office in the western provinces he brought Lady Liu with him.
translations.idiomatic: When he took up his post in the western provinces, he brought Lady Liu with him.

sentences.zh: 洪之素非廉清，每多受納。

translations.literal: Hongzhi had never been honest and clean; he frequently accepted many bribes.
translations.idiomatic: Hongzhi had never been honest; he frequently accepted bribes.

sentences.zh: 時高祖始建祿制，法禁嚴峻，司察所聞，無不窮糾。

translations.literal: At that time Emperor Gaozu had just established the salary system; laws and prohibitions were severe, and whatever the inspectors heard they pursued to the end.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gaozu had just instituted the salary system; laws were strict, and inspectors pursued every report to its conclusion.

sentences.zh: 遂鎖洪之赴京。

translations.literal: Hongzhi was therefore shackled and sent to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Hongzhi was shackled and escorted to the capital.

sentences.zh: 高祖臨太華，庭集羣官，有司奏洪之受贓狼藉，又以酷暴。

translations.literal: Emperor Gaozu came to Taihua; officials were assembled in the court. The responsible offices reported that Hongzhi's acceptance of bribes was flagrant, and that he was also cruel and violent.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gaozu convened the court at Taihua Hall. The authorities reported that Hongzhi's bribery was rampant and that he was also brutal.

sentences.zh: 高祖親臨數之，以其大臣，聽在家自裁。

translations.literal: Emperor Gaozu personally came forward and rebuked him; because he was a great minister, he was permitted to take his own life at home.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gaozu rebuked him in person; because he was a senior minister, he was permitted to take his own life at home.

sentences.zh: 洪之志性慷慨，多所堪忍，疹疾灸療，艾炷圍將二寸，首足十餘處，一時俱下，而言笑自若，接賓不輟。

translations.literal: Hongzhi's disposition was bold and generous and he could endure much. When he was treated for rash illness by moxibustion, the moxa cones were nearly two inches around; more than ten places on head and limbs received them all at once, yet he spoke and laughed as usual and did not cease receiving guests.
translations.idiomatic: Hongzhi was bold and long-suffering. When treated for skin ailments by moxibustion, cones nearly two inches across were applied to more than ten points on his head and limbs all at once, yet he conversed and laughed as usual and never ceased receiving guests.

sentences.zh: 及臨自盡，沐浴換衣。

translations.literal: When the time came for him to take his own life, he bathed and changed his clothes.
translations.idiomatic: When the time came to take his own life, he bathed and changed his garments.

sentences.zh: 防卒扶持，將出却入，遍遶家庭，如是再三，泣歎良久，乃臥而引藥。

translations.literal: Guards supported him as he was about to go out, then turned back in, walked all around the household—thus three times—wept and sighed for a long while, then lay down and took the poison.
translations.idiomatic: Supported by guards, he started to leave, then turned back, walked through his entire household three times, wept and sighed at length, then lay down and drank the poison.

sentences.zh: 始洪之託為元后兄，公私自同外戚。

translations.literal: At first Hongzhi had pretended to be the Empress Yuan's brother and had privately enjoyed the privileges of imperial kin by marriage.
translations.idiomatic: At first Hongzhi had passed himself off as Empress Yuan's brother and privately enjoyed the privileges of imperial kin.

sentences.zh: 至此罪後，高祖乃稍對百官辨其誣假，而諸李猶善相視，恩紀如親。

translations.literal: After this offense Emperor Gaozu gradually explained to the officials his deception, yet the various Lis still treated one another well and their bonds of kindness remained as among kin.
translations.idiomatic: After his conviction Emperor Gaozu gradually explained to the officials the fraud he had perpetrated, yet the Li clan still treated one another with affection, their bonds as close as kin.

sentences.zh: 洪之始見元后，計年為兄。

translations.literal: When Hongzhi first met the Empress Yuan, he reckoned by age that he was her elder brother.
translations.idiomatic: When Hongzhi first met Empress Yuan, he calculated by age that he was her elder brother.

sentences.zh: 及珍之等至，洪之以元后素定長幼，其呼拜坐皆如家人。

translations.literal: When Zhenzhi and the others arrived, Hongzhi, because the Empress Yuan had long since fixed their seniority, addressed them, bowed, and seated himself all as among family.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhenzhi and the others arrived, Hongzhi—relying on the seniority Empress Yuan had long since established—greeted them with the ease of family, bowing and taking his seat as among kin.

sentences.zh: 暮年數延攜之宴飲，醉酣之後，攜之時或言及本末，洪之則起而加敬，笑語自若。

translations.literal: In his later years he often invited Xiezhi to banquets. After deep drunkenness Xiezhi would sometimes speak of how things had begun and ended; Hongzhi would rise and show added respect, yet laugh and talk as usual.
translations.idiomatic: In his later years he often invited Xiezhi to feasts. When drunk, Xiezhi would sometimes recount how their relationship had begun; Hongzhi would rise and show added deference, yet converse and laugh as usual.

sentences.zh: 富貴赫弈，當舅戚之家，遂棄宗專附珍之等。

translations.literal: His wealth and rank blazed brilliantly; as a household of maternal imperial kin, he abandoned his own clan and attached himself solely to Zhenzhi and the others.
translations.idiomatic: His wealth and rank blazed brilliantly; as a household of imperial kin by marriage, he abandoned his own clan and attached himself exclusively to Zhenzhi and his brothers.

sentences.zh: 後頗存振本屬，而猶不顯然。

translations.literal: Later he somewhat sought to revive his original clan affiliation, but still not openly.
translations.idiomatic: Later he made some effort to restore ties with his original clan, but only discreetly.

sentences.zh: 劉氏四子，長子神自有傳。

translations.literal: Lady Liu had four sons; the eldest son Shen has his own biography.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Liu had four sons; the eldest, Shen, has his own biography.

sentences.zh: 高遵，字世禮，勃海蓚人。

translations.literal: Gao Zun, courtesy name Shili, was a man of Su in Bohai.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Zun, courtesy name Shili, was a native of Su in Bohai.

sentences.zh: 父濟，滄水太守。

translations.literal: His father Ji was Administrator of Cangshui.
translations.idiomatic: His father Ji served as Administrator of Cangshui.

sentences.zh: 遵賤出，兄矯等常欺侮之。

translations.literal: Zun was born of a low-status mother; his elder brother Jiao and the others often bullied him.
translations.idiomatic: Zun was born of a concubine; his elder brother Jiao and the others often bullied him.

sentences.zh: 及父亡，不令在喪位。

translations.literal: When his father died they did not allow him to take his place in mourning.
translations.idiomatic: When his father died they did not permit him to take his proper place in the mourning rites.

sentences.zh: 遵遂馳赴平城，歸從祖兄中書令允。

translations.literal: Zun thereupon galloped to Pingcheng and went to his father's cousin, the Director of the Secretariat Yun.
translations.idiomatic: Zun galloped to Pingcheng and sought out his father's cousin Yun, Director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 允乃為遵父舉哀，以遵為喪主，京邑無不弔集，朝貴咸識之。

translations.literal: Yun then conducted mourning for Zun's father, made Zun chief mourner, and everyone in the capital came to offer condolences; the court nobility all came to know him.
translations.idiomatic: Yun conducted mourning for Zun's father and installed Zun as chief mourner; the entire capital came to pay condolences, and the court elite all came to know him.

sentences.zh: 徐歸奔赴。

translations.literal: Only later did he return to attend the funeral.
translations.idiomatic: Only afterward did he return home for the funeral.

sentences.zh: 免喪，允為營宦路，得補樂浪王侍郎。

translations.literal: When mourning ended, Yun arranged an official career for him, and he was appointed Attendant to the Prince of Lelang.
translations.idiomatic: When mourning ended, Yun secured an official post for him, and he was appointed Attendant to the Prince of Lelang.

sentences.zh: 遵感成益之恩，事允如諸父。

translations.literal: Zun was grateful for the benefit Yun had conferred and served Yun as he would an uncle.
translations.idiomatic: Grateful for the benefit Yun had conferred, Zun served him as he would an uncle.

sentences.zh: 涉歷文史，頗有筆札，進中書侍郎。

translations.literal: He studied literature and history and possessed considerable skill with the brush; he was promoted to Attendant of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He studied literature and history and was skilled with the pen; he was promoted to Attendant of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 詣長安，刊燕宣王廟碑，進爵安昌子。

translations.literal: He went to Chang'an and carved the temple stele for Prince Xuan of Yan, and was advanced to Viscount of Anchang.
translations.idiomatic: He went to Chang'an to carve the temple stele for Prince Xuan of Yan and was ennobled as Viscount of Anchang.

sentences.zh: 及新製衣冠，高祖恭薦宗廟，遵形貌莊潔，音氣雄暢，常兼太祝令，跪贊禮事，為俯仰之節，粗合儀矩。

translations.literal: When new caps and robes were made and Emperor Gaozu reverently offered sacrifice at the ancestral temple, Zun's bearing was dignified and pure, his voice strong and clear. He regularly served concurrently as Director of Grand Sacrifices, kneeling to intone the ritual proceedings and performing the movements of bowing and rising, roughly conforming to ceremonial norms.
translations.idiomatic: When new ceremonial robes were introduced and Emperor Gaozu offered sacrifice at the ancestral temple, Zun's bearing was dignified and his voice resonant. He regularly served as Director of Grand Sacrifices, kneeling to intone the rituals and performing the prescribed movements of obeisance, roughly in accord with ceremonial propriety.

sentences.zh: 由是高祖識待之。

translations.literal: Hence Emperor Gaozu came to know and favor him.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gaozu thereby came to notice and favor him.

sentences.zh: 後與游明根、高閭、李沖入議律令，親對御坐，時有陳奏。

translations.literal: Later, together with You Minggen, Gao Lü, and Li Chong, he entered deliberation on laws and statutes, speaking face to face before the imperial seat and sometimes offering memorials.
translations.idiomatic: Later, together with You Minggen, Gao Lü, and Li Chong, he participated in drafting laws and statutes, speaking before the emperor and occasionally offering proposals.

sentences.zh: 以積年之勞，賜粟帛牛馬。

translations.literal: For accumulated years of service he was granted grain, silks, cattle, and horses.
translations.idiomatic: For years of accumulated service he was rewarded with grain, silk, cattle, and horses.

sentences.zh: 出為立忠將軍、齊州刺史。

translations.literal: He went out as General Who Establishes Loyalty and Governor of Qizhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed General Who Establishes Loyalty and Governor of Qizhou.

sentences.zh: 建節歷本州，宗鄉改觀，而矯等彌妬毀之。

translations.literal: Bearing the staff of authority he passed through his home province; clansmen and townsfolk changed their view of him, yet Jiao and the others only grew more jealous and slandered him.
translations.idiomatic: Bearing the staff of authority he toured his home province; clansmen and neighbors changed their opinion of him, yet Jiao and the others grew only more envious and slandered him.

sentences.zh: 遵性不廉清，在中書時，每假歸山東，必借備騾馬，將從百餘。

translations.literal: Zun's character was not honest and clean. While at the Secretariat, whenever he took leave to return to Shandong he invariably requisitioned mules and horses and had more than a hundred attendants.
translations.idiomatic: Zun was not honest. While serving at the Secretariat, whenever he took leave to return to Shandong he requisitioned mules and horses and traveled with more than a hundred attendants.

sentences.zh: 屯逼民家求絲縑，不滿意則詬罵不去，強相徵求。

translations.literal: He quartered troops and pressed common households for silk and fine cloth; if not satisfied he reviled them and would not leave, forcibly extorting supplies.
translations.idiomatic: He billeted troops on common households and demanded silk and fine cloth; if dissatisfied he cursed them and refused to leave, forcibly extorting goods.

sentences.zh: 旬月之間，縑布千數。

translations.literal: Within a month or so he accumulated several thousand bolts of silk cloth.
translations.idiomatic: Within a month he accumulated several thousand bolts of silk.

sentences.zh: 邦邑苦之。

translations.literal: The towns and districts suffered from it.
translations.idiomatic: The towns and districts suffered grievously.

sentences.zh: 遵既臨州，本意未弭，選召僚吏，多所取納。

translations.literal: Once Zun took up the governorship his original intent was not quelled; in selecting and summoning subordinate officials he accepted many bribes.
translations.idiomatic: Once Zun took office as governor his greed was unchecked; in appointing subordinates he accepted numerous bribes.

sentences.zh: 又其妻明氏家在齊州，母弟舅甥共相憑屬，爭求貨利，嚴暴非理，殺害甚多。

translations.literal: Moreover, his wife Lady Ming's family was in Qizhou; mother, younger brothers, maternal uncles, and nephews relied on one another, vied for profit, acted with harsh violence beyond reason, and killed many.
translations.idiomatic: His wife Lady Ming's family lived in Qizhou; her mother, brothers, uncles, and nephews relied on one another, vied for profit, acted with brutal violence, and killed many.

sentences.zh: 貪酷之響，帝頗聞之。

translations.literal: Reports of his greed and cruelty reached the emperor rather fully.
translations.idiomatic: Reports of his greed and cruelty reached the emperor.

sentences.zh: 及車駕幸鄴，遵自州來朝，會有赦宥。

translations.literal: When the imperial carriage visited Ye, Zun came from his province to court; it happened that there was a general amnesty.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor visited Ye, Zun came from his province to court; a general amnesty happened to be in effect.

sentences.zh: 遵臨還州，請辭帝於行宮，引見誚讓之。

translations.literal: As Zun was about to return to his province he requested leave of the emperor at the traveling palace; the emperor received him and rebuked him.
translations.idiomatic: As Zun prepared to return to his province he took leave of the emperor at the traveling palace; the emperor received him and rebuked him sharply.

sentences.zh: 遵自陳無負，帝厲聲曰：「若無遷都赦，必無高遵矣！

translations.literal: Zun declared himself innocent, but the emperor said in a harsh voice: "Were it not for the amnesty on the move of the capital, there would certainly be no Gao Zun left!
translations.idiomatic: Zun protested his innocence, but the emperor said harshly: "Were it not for the amnesty proclaimed at the capital's relocation, Gao Zun would certainly be dead!

sentences.zh: 又卿非惟貪惏，又虐於刑法，謂何如濟陰王，猶不免於法。

translations.literal: Moreover, you are not only greedy but also cruel in penal law—what do you think of the Prince of Jiyin? Even he could not escape the law.
translations.idiomatic: You are not only greedy but brutal in your application of the law—consider the Prince of Jiyin: even he could not escape punishment.

sentences.zh: 卿何人，而為此行！

translations.literal: Who are you, to act in this way!
translations.idiomatic: Who are you to behave in this fashion!

sentences.zh: 自今宜自謹約。」

translations.literal: From now on you should restrain yourself."
translations.idiomatic: Henceforth you must restrain yourself."

sentences.zh: 還州，仍不悛革。

translations.literal: When he returned to his province he still did not repent or reform.
translations.idiomatic: After returning to his province he still did not reform.

sentences.zh: 齊州人孟僧振至洛訟遵。

translations.literal: Meng Sengzhen of Qizhou went to Luoyang to sue Zun.
translations.idiomatic: Meng Sengzhen of Qizhou traveled to Luoyang to bring suit against Zun.

sentences.zh: 詔廷尉少卿劉述窮鞫，皆如所訴。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Vice Director of the Court of Judicial Review Liu Shu to investigate to the end; everything was as alleged.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered Vice Director Liu Shu of the Court of Judicial Review to investigate thoroughly; every charge proved true.

sentences.zh: 先是，沙門道登過遵，遵以道登荷寵於高祖，多奉以貨，深託仗之。

translations.literal: Earlier the monk Daodeng had visited Zun. Zun, because Daodeng enjoyed favor from Emperor Gaozu, presented him with many gifts and relied on him deeply.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier the monk Daodeng had visited Zun. Knowing that Daodeng enjoyed Emperor Gaozu's favor, Zun lavished gifts on him and placed great trust in him.

sentences.zh: 道登屢因言次申啟救遵，帝不省納，遂詔述賜遵死。

translations.literal: Daodeng repeatedly seized occasions of conversation to plead for Zun's life, but the emperor would not heed him; an edict then ordered Shu to grant Zun death.
translations.idiomatic: Daodeng repeatedly interceded for Zun, but the emperor would not listen; an edict then ordered Shu to sentence Zun to death.

sentences.zh: 時遵子元榮詣洛訟冤，猶恃道登，不時還赴。

translations.literal: At that time Zun's son Yuanrong went to Luoyang to plead his father's innocence; still trusting in Daodeng, he did not return in time.
translations.idiomatic: Zun's son Yuanrong went to Luoyang to plead his father's case; still trusting in Daodeng, he did not return in time.

sentences.zh: 道登知事決，方乃遣之。

translations.literal: When Daodeng knew the matter was settled, only then did he send him back.
translations.idiomatic: Only when Daodeng knew the outcome was settled did he send him back.

sentences.zh: 遵恨其妻，不與訣，別處沐浴，引椒而死。

translations.literal: Zun hated his wife and did not bid her farewell; he bathed elsewhere and took pepper poison to die.
translations.idiomatic: Zun hated his wife and would not bid her farewell; he bathed in a separate room and took poison.

sentences.zh: 元榮，學尚有文才，長於几案。

translations.literal: Yuanrong was learned and possessed literary talent; he excelled at desk work.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanrong was learned and gifted with literary talent; he excelled at administrative work.

sentences.zh: 位兼尚書右丞，為西道行臺，至高平鎮，遇城翻被害。

translations.literal: He held the concurrent post of Right Vice Director of the Secretariat and served on the Western Route Staff; when he reached Gaoping garrison the city rebelled and he was killed.
translations.idiomatic: He served concurrently as Right Vice Director of the Secretariat and on the Western Route Staff; when he reached Gaoping garrison the city rebelled and he was killed.

sentences.zh: 遵弟次文，雖無位官而貲產巨萬。

translations.literal: Zun's younger brother Ciwen, though without official rank, possessed wealth of tens of thousands.
translations.idiomatic: Zun's younger brother Ciwen, though he held no office, possessed vast wealth.

sentences.zh: 遵每責其財，又結憾於遵，吉凶不相往反。

translations.literal: Zun constantly demanded his wealth from him; they also harbored resentment toward each other and did not visit one another on occasions of joy or mourning.
translations.idiomatic: Zun constantly demanded money from him; they nursed mutual resentment and did not visit one another on occasions of joy or mourning.

sentences.zh: 時論責之。

translations.literal: Contemporary opinion censured him.
translations.idiomatic: Public opinion censured him.

sentences.zh: 張赦提，中山安喜人也。

translations.literal: Zhang Sheti was a man of Anxi in Zhongshan.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Sheti was a native of Anxi in Zhongshan.

sentences.zh: 性雄武，有規畫。

translations.literal: His nature was bold and martial, and he possessed strategic planning.
translations.idiomatic: He was bold and martial, with a talent for strategy.

sentences.zh: 初為虎賁中郎。

translations.literal: At first he served as Central Commander of the Tiger Guards.
translations.idiomatic: He first served as Central Commander of the Tiger Guards.

sentences.zh: 時京畿盜魁自稱豹子、虎子，並善弓馬，遂領逃連及諸畜牧者，[2]各為部帥，於靈丘、雁門間聚為劫害。

translations.literal: At that time the bandit chiefs of the capital region called themselves Leopard and Tiger; both were skilled with bow and horse. They then led fugitives and various herdsmen, each as a troop leader, gathering between Lingqiu and Yanmen to plunder.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the bandit chiefs of the capital region called themselves Leopard and Tiger; both were skilled horsemen and archers. They gathered fugitives and herdsmen as troop leaders and plundered between Lingqiu and Yanmen.

sentences.zh: 至乃斬人首，射其口，刺人臍，引腸遶樹而共射之，以為戲笑。

translations.literal: They would even cut off people's heads, shoot at their mouths, stab people's navels, draw out the intestines and wrap them around trees, then shoot at them together for sport and laughter.
translations.idiomatic: They would cut off heads, shoot arrows into mouths, stab navels, draw out intestines and wrap them around trees, then shoot at them for sport.

sentences.zh: 其為暴酷如此。

translations.literal: Their violence and cruelty were such as this.
translations.idiomatic: Such was the brutality of their conduct.

sentences.zh: 軍騎掩㨞，久弗能獲，行者患焉。

translations.literal: Cavalry raided and pursued them but for a long time could not capture them; travelers suffered from it.
translations.idiomatic: Government cavalry pursued them but for a long time could not capture them; travelers lived in fear.

sentences.zh: 赦提設防遏追窮之計，宰司善之，以赦提為逐賊軍將。

translations.literal: Sheti devised plans for defense, interception, pursuit, and thorough extermination; the chief ministers approved and appointed Sheti General for Pursuit of Bandits.
translations.idiomatic: Sheti devised plans to block, pursue, and exterminate the bandits; the chief ministers approved and appointed him General for Pursuit of Bandits.

sentences.zh: 乃求驍勇追之，未幾而獲虎子、豹子及其黨與。

translations.literal: He then sought fierce warriors to pursue them, and before long captured Tiger, Leopard, and their followers.
translations.idiomatic: He recruited fierce warriors to pursue them and soon captured Tiger, Leopard, and their followers.

sentences.zh: 盡送京師，斬於闕下，自是清靜。

translations.literal: All were sent to the capital and beheaded below the palace gates; thereafter the region was peaceful.
translations.idiomatic: All were sent to the capital and beheaded at the palace gates; thereafter the region was at peace.

sentences.zh: 其靈丘羅思祖宗門豪溢，家處隘險，多止亡命，與之為劫。

translations.literal: In Lingqiu the Luo clan of Sizu was a powerful and wealthy household dwelling in narrow defiles; many fugitives lodged with them and joined in robbery.
translations.idiomatic: In Lingqiu the Luo clan of Sizu was a powerful household in a rugged stronghold; many fugitives sheltered with them and joined in banditry.

sentences.zh: 顯祖怒之，孥戮其家。

translations.literal: Emperor Xianzu was enraged and exterminated the entire family.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xianzu was enraged and exterminated the entire clan.

sentences.zh: 而思祖家黨，相率寇盜。

translations.literal: Yet Sizu's kinsmen and followers banded together in raiding and robbery.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Sizu's kinsmen and followers banded together as bandits.

sentences.zh: 赦提應募求捕逐，乃以赦提為游徼軍將，前後禽獲，殺之略盡。

translations.literal: Sheti volunteered to hunt and pursue them and was appointed General of Patrol Forces; in successive campaigns he captured them and killed nearly all.
translations.idiomatic: Sheti volunteered to hunt them down and was appointed General of Patrol Forces; in successive campaigns he captured and killed nearly all of them.

sentences.zh: 因而濫有屠害，尤為忍酷。

translations.literal: In the process he indiscriminately slaughtered many, and was especially cruel and ruthless.
translations.idiomatic: In the process he indiscriminately slaughtered many, showing exceptional cruelty.

sentences.zh: 既資前稱，又藉此功，除冠軍將軍、幽州刺史，假安喜侯。

translations.literal: Relying on his earlier reputation and this achievement, he was appointed General Who Conquers the Enemy and Governor of Youzhou, with the provisional title Marquis of Anxi.
translations.idiomatic: On the strength of his earlier reputation and this achievement, he was appointed General Who Conquers the Enemy and Governor of Youzhou, with the provisional title Marquis of Anxi.

sentences.zh: 赦提克己厲約，遂有清稱。

translations.literal: Sheti restrained himself and practiced austerity, and thereby gained a reputation for integrity.
translations.idiomatic: Sheti disciplined himself and practiced austerity, earning a reputation for integrity.

sentences.zh: 後頗縱妻段氏，多有受納，令僧尼因事通請，貪虐流聞。

translations.literal: Later he indulged his wife Lady Duan rather fully; there were many bribes, and he had monks and nuns intercede on various matters; reports of greed and cruelty spread.
translations.idiomatic: Later he indulged his wife Lady Duan; bribes were frequent, and he used monks and nuns as intermediaries for favors; reports of greed and cruelty spread widely.

sentences.zh: 中散李真香出使幽州，採訪牧守政績。

translations.literal: Palace Attendant Li Zhenxiang went on mission to Youzhou to investigate the achievements of provincial governors.
translations.idiomatic: Palace Attendant Li Zhenxiang was sent to Youzhou to investigate the conduct of provincial governors.

sentences.zh: 真香驗案其罪，赦提懼死欲逃。

translations.literal: Zhenxiang verified and prosecuted his crimes; Sheti, fearing death, wished to flee.
translations.idiomatic: Zhenxiang verified his crimes; Sheti, fearing execution, planned to flee.

sentences.zh: 其妻姑為太尉、東陽王丕妻，恃丕親貴，自許詣丕申訴求助，謂赦提曰：「當為訴理，幸得申雪，願且寬憂，不為異計。」

translations.literal: His wife's aunt was the wife of the Grand Commandant, Prince of Dongyang Pi; relying on Pi's kinship and rank, she promised to go to Pi to plead and seek help, telling Sheti: "I shall plead your case; if we can clear your name, I hope you will set aside your worries for now and make no other plans."
translations.idiomatic: His wife's aunt was married to Grand Commandant Pi, Prince of Dongyang; relying on Pi's rank and connections, she promised to appeal to him on Sheti's behalf, telling Sheti: "I shall plead your case; if we can clear your name, set aside your worries for now and make no other plans."

sentences.zh: 赦提以此差自解慰。

translations.literal: Sheti was somewhat relieved and comforted by this.
translations.idiomatic: Sheti was somewhat reassured by this.

sentences.zh: 段乃陳列真香昔嘗因假而過幽州，知赦提有好牛，從索不果。

translations.literal: Lady Duan then set forth that Zhenxiang had once passed through Youzhou on leave, knew Sheti had a fine ox, asked for it but failed to obtain it.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Duan then argued that Zhenxiang had once passed through Youzhou on leave, knew Sheti owned a fine ox, had asked for it and been refused.

sentences.zh: 今臺使心協前事，[3]故威逼部下，拷楚過極，橫以無辜，證成誣罪。

translations.literal: Now the imperial envoy bore a grudge over that earlier matter; therefore he coerced subordinates, tortured them beyond all bounds, and falsely charged the innocent to fabricate a trumped-up crime.
translations.idiomatic: Now the imperial envoy still harbored resentment over that earlier affair; he coerced subordinates, tortured them excessively, and fabricated charges against the innocent.

sentences.zh: 執事恐有不盡，使駕部令趙秦州重往究訊。

translations.literal: The authorities, fearing the investigation was incomplete, sent Director of the Imperial Carriage Office Zhao of Qinzhou to investigate again.
translations.idiomatic: The authorities, fearing the investigation was incomplete, sent Director Zhao of the Imperial Carriage Office to reinvestigate.

sentences.zh: 事伏如前，處赦提大辟。

translations.literal: The facts were as before; Sheti was sentenced to the death penalty.
translations.idiomatic: The facts were confirmed as before; Sheti was sentenced to death.

sentences.zh: 高祖詔賜死於第。

translations.literal: Emperor Gaozu ordered that he be granted death at his residence.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gaozu ordered that he be permitted to take his own life at home.

sentences.zh: 將就盡，召妻而責之曰：「貪濁穢吾者卿也，又安吾而不得免禍，九泉之下當為仇讎矣。」

translations.literal: As he was about to die he summoned his wife and rebuked her: "It was you who defiled me with greed and corruption, yet you also comforted me and could not save me from disaster; in the nine springs below we shall be enemies."
translations.idiomatic: As death approached he summoned his wife and rebuked her: "You defiled me with your greed, yet you comforted me and could not save me from ruin; in the grave we shall be enemies."

sentences.zh: 又有華山太守趙霸，酷暴非理。

translations.literal: There was also Zhao Ba, Administrator of Huashan, cruel and violent beyond reason.
translations.idiomatic: There was also Zhao Ba, Administrator of Huashan, whose cruelty exceeded all bounds.

sentences.zh: 大使崔光奏霸云：「不遵憲度，威虐任情，至乃手擊吏人，僚屬奔走。

translations.literal: Imperial Commissioner Cui Guang memorialized against Ba, saying: "He does not observe the laws and statutes; he exercises authority and cruelty as he pleases, even to the point of striking clerks and attendants with his own hands, so that subordinates flee in panic.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial Commissioner Cui Guang memorialized against Ba: "He disregards the laws, exercises cruelty at will, even strikes clerks with his own hands, and drives his subordinates to flee in terror.

sentences.zh: 不可以君人字下，納之軌物，輒禁止在州。」

translations.literal: He cannot be allowed to rule over the people and be received within the norms of governance; he should forthwith be detained in the province."
translations.idiomatic: He cannot be permitted to govern the people or remain within the bounds of proper conduct; he should be detained in the province at once."

sentences.zh: 詔免所居官。

translations.literal: An edict removed him from his office.
translations.idiomatic: An edict dismissed him from office.

sentences.zh: 羊祉，字靈祐，太山鉅平人，晉太僕卿琇之六世孫也。

translations.literal: Yang Zhi, courtesy name Lingyou, was a man of Juping in Taishan, sixth-generation descendant of Xiu, Grand Master of the Imperial Stud in Jin.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Zhi, courtesy name Lingyou, was a native of Juping in Taishan and sixth-generation descendant of Xiu, Grand Master of the Imperial Stud under the Jin.

sentences.zh: 父規之，宋任城令。

translations.literal: His father Guizhi was Magistrate of Rencheng under Song.
translations.idiomatic: His father Guizhi served as Magistrate of Rencheng under the Liu Song.

sentences.zh: 世祖南討至鄒山，規之與魯郡太守崔邪利及其屬縣徐通、愛猛之等俱降，賜爵鉅平子，拜雁門太守。

translations.literal: When Emperor Shizu campaigned south to Zou Mountain, Guizhi together with Cui Xieli, Administrator of Lu Commandery, and Xu Tong, Ai Mengzhi, and others of the subordinate counties all surrendered; he was granted the title Viscount of Juping and appointed Administrator of Yanmen.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Shizu campaigned south to Zou Mountain, Guizhi surrendered together with Cui Xieli, Administrator of Lu, and officials of subordinate counties including Xu Tong and Ai Mengzhi; he was ennobled as Viscount of Juping and appointed Administrator of Yanmen.

sentences.zh: 祉性剛愎，好刑名，為司空令輔國長史，[4]襲爵鉅平子。

translations.literal: Zhi's nature was stubborn and obstinate; he favored penal law. He served as Chief Aide to the Support-the-State Army under the Minister of Works and inherited the title Viscount of Juping.
translations.idiomatic: Zhi was stubborn and obstinate, with a fondness for penal law. He served as Chief Aide to the Support-the-State Army under the Minister of Works and inherited the title Viscount of Juping.

sentences.zh: 侵盜公資，私營居宅，有司案之抵死，高祖特恕遠徙。

translations.literal: He embezzled public funds and built a private residence; the responsible offices prosecuted him to the death penalty, but Emperor Gaozu specially pardoned him and exiled him to a distant place.
translations.idiomatic: He embezzled public funds and built a private residence; the authorities prosecuted him for a capital offense, but Emperor Gaozu specially pardoned him and exiled him to a distant region.

sentences.zh: 後還。

translations.literal: Later he returned.
translations.idiomatic: He was later permitted to return.

sentences.zh: 景明初，為將作都將，加左軍將軍。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Jingming era he served as Director of Palace Construction and was given the additional title General of the Left Army.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Jingming era he served as Director of Palace Construction with the additional title General of the Left Army.

sentences.zh: 四年，持節為梁州軍司，討叛氐。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he bore the staff of authority as Military Commissioner of Liangzhou to campaign against rebellious Di.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year he bore the staff of authority as Military Commissioner of Liangzhou to campaign against rebellious Di tribes.

sentences.zh: 正始二年，王師伐蜀，以祉假節、龍驤將軍、益州刺史，出劍閣而還。

translations.literal: In the second year of Zhengshi the royal army campaigned against Shu; Zhi was given provisional authority as General of the Flying Dragon and Governor of Yizhou, advanced through Jian'ge Pass and returned.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Zhengshi the imperial army campaigned against Shu; Zhi was appointed provisional General of the Flying Dragon and Governor of Yizhou, advanced through Jian'ge Pass, and returned.

sentences.zh: 又以本將軍為秦梁二州刺史，加征虜將軍。

translations.literal: He was again appointed with his original rank as General as Governor of the two provinces Qin and Liang, with the additional title General Who Subdues the Barbarians.
translations.idiomatic: He was again appointed Governor of Qin and Liang provinces with his original rank, and given the additional title General Who Subdues the Barbarians.

sentences.zh: 天性酷忍，又不清潔。

translations.literal: By nature he was cruel and ruthless, and also not honest.
translations.idiomatic: By nature he was cruel and dishonest.

sentences.zh: 坐掠人為奴婢，為御史中尉王顯所彈免。

translations.literal: He was impeached and dismissed by Director of the Imperial Secretariat Wang Xian for seizing people as slaves.
translations.idiomatic: He was impeached and dismissed by Director of the Imperial Secretariat Wang Xian for seizing people as slaves.

sentences.zh: 高肇南征，祉復被起為光祿大夫、假平南將軍，持節領步騎三萬先驅趣涪。

translations.literal: When Gao Zhao campaigned south, Zhi was again summoned as Grand Master for Splendid Happiness and provisional General Who Pacifies the South, bearing the staff of authority to lead thirty thousand infantry and cavalry as vanguard hurrying to Fu.
translations.idiomatic: When Gao Zhao campaigned south, Zhi was again summoned as Grand Master for Splendid Happiness and provisional General Who Pacifies the South, bearing the staff of authority to lead thirty thousand infantry and cavalry as vanguard toward Fu.

sentences.zh: 未至，世宗崩，班師。

translations.literal: Before he arrived, Emperor Shizong died and the army withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Before he arrived, Emperor Shizong died and the army withdrew.

sentences.zh: 夜中引軍，山有二徑，軍人迷而失路。

translations.literal: He led the army by night; the mountain had two paths, and the soldiers lost their way in confusion.
translations.idiomatic: He led the army by night; the mountain had two paths, and the soldiers lost their way.

sentences.zh: 祉便斬隊副楊明達，梟首路側。

translations.literal: Zhi thereupon beheaded the squad deputy Yang Mingda and displayed his head beside the road.
translations.idiomatic: Zhi immediately beheaded squad deputy Yang Mingda and displayed his head beside the road.

sentences.zh: 為中尉元昭所劾，會赦免。

translations.literal: He was impeached by Director Yuan Zhao and was pardoned when an amnesty was proclaimed.
translations.idiomatic: He was impeached by Director Yuan Zhao but was pardoned when an amnesty was proclaimed.

sentences.zh: 後加平北將軍，未拜而卒。

translations.literal: Later he was given the additional title General Who Pacifies the North but died before assuming the post.
translations.idiomatic: He was later given the additional title General Who Pacifies the North but died before assuming the post.

sentences.zh: 贈安東將軍、兗州刺史。

translations.literal: He was posthumously granted General Who Pacifies the East and Governor of Yanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously granted the title General Who Pacifies the East and Governor of Yanzhou.

sentences.zh: 太常少卿元端、博士劉臺龍議諡曰：「祉志存埋輪，不避強禦。

translations.literal: Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices Yuan Duan and Erudite Liu Tailong proposed the posthumous title, saying: "Zhi's will was set on burying the wheel—he did not avoid the powerful.
translations.idiomatic: Vice Director Yuan Duan of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and Erudite Liu Tailong proposed the posthumous title, saying: "Zhi was resolved to curb abuse of power and did not shrink from the mighty.

sentences.zh: 及贊戎律，熊武斯裁，仗節撫藩，邊夷識德，化沾殊類，襁負懷仁。

translations.literal: When he assisted in military affairs his martial prowess was displayed; bearing the staff he pacified the frontier, frontier peoples recognized his virtue, his transforming influence reached diverse peoples, and infants in swaddling clothes cherished his benevolence.
translations.idiomatic: In military affairs he displayed martial prowess; bearing the staff he pacified the frontier, where frontier peoples recognized his virtue; his transforming influence reached all peoples, and even infants cherished his benevolence.

sentences.zh: 謹依諡法，布德行剛曰『景』，宜諡為景。」

translations.literal: According to the posthumous-title law, 'displaying virtue with a firm disposition' is Jing; he should be given the posthumous title Jing."
translations.idiomatic: According to the law of posthumous titles, 'displaying virtue with firm resolve' is Jing; he should be given the posthumous title Jing."

sentences.zh: 侍中侯剛、給事黃門侍郎元纂等駁曰：「臣聞惟名與器，弗可妄假，定諡準行，必當其迹。

translations.literal: Attendant-in-Ordinary Hou Gang, Attendant Gentleman of the Yellow Gate Yuan Zuan, and others rebutted, saying: "We have heard that names and insignia must not be lightly bestowed; in fixing a posthumous title according to conduct, it must match the facts.
translations.idiomatic: Attendant-in-Ordinary Hou Gang, Attendant Gentleman of the Yellow Gate Yuan Zuan, and others objected: "Names and honors must not be lightly bestowed; a posthumous title must match the man's actual conduct.

sentences.zh: 案祉志性急酷，所在過威，布德罕聞，暴聲屢發。

translations.literal: Investigation shows that Zhi's disposition was harsh and cruel; wherever he served he exceeded in severity; reports of his dispensing virtue were rarely heard, while reports of his violence arose repeatedly.
translations.idiomatic: Investigation shows that Zhi was harsh and cruel; wherever he served he exceeded all bounds of severity; virtue was rarely attributed to him, while reports of violence arose repeatedly.

sentences.zh: 而禮官虛述，諡之為『景』，非直失於一人，實毀朝則。

translations.literal: Yet the ritual officials have described him falsely and would give him the title Jing; this is not merely an error concerning one man—it truly damages the standards of the court.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the ritual officials have described him falsely and would give him the title Jing; this is not merely an error concerning one man—it damages the standards of the court itself.

sentences.zh: 請還付外準行，更量虛實。」

translations.literal: We request that the matter be returned to the outer offices to determine conduct according to the facts, and that truth and falsehood be weighed anew."
translations.idiomatic: We request that the matter be returned to the outer offices for reassessment according to the facts."

sentences.zh: 靈太后令曰：「依駁更議。」

translations.literal: Empress Dowager Ling ordered: "In accordance with the rebuttal, deliberate again."
translations.idiomatic: Empress Dowager Ling ordered: "In accordance with the objection, deliberate again."

sentences.zh: 元端、臺龍上言：「竊惟諡者行之迹，狀者迹之稱。

translations.literal: Yuan Duan and Tailong submitted: "We consider that the posthumous title is the trace of conduct, and the memorial of conduct is the designation of that trace.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Duan and Tailong submitted: "The posthumous title records a man's conduct; the memorial of conduct is the designation of that record.

sentences.zh: 然尚書銓衡是司，釐品庶物，若狀與跡乖，應抑而不受，錄其實狀，然後下寺，依諡法準狀科上。

translations.literal: Yet the Secretariat is charged with weighing and balancing, ordering all things; if the memorial of conduct and the actual trace diverge, it should be suppressed and not accepted, the true conduct recorded, and only then sent down to the temple offices to fix the title according to the law based on the memorial.
translations.idiomatic: The Secretariat is charged with evaluating conduct; if the memorial and the facts diverge, it should be rejected, the true conduct recorded, and only then sent to the temple offices to fix the title according to law.

sentences.zh: 豈有捨其行迹，外有所求，去狀去稱，將何所準？

translations.literal: How can one abandon his conduct and trace, seek something outside, discard the memorial and the designation—what then would serve as the standard?
translations.idiomatic: How can one abandon the record of his conduct, seek external grounds, and discard both memorial and designation—what standard would remain?

sentences.zh: 檢祉以母老辭藩，乃降手詔云：『卿綏撫有年，聲實兼著，安邊寧境，實稱朝望。』

translations.literal: Examination shows that when Zhi resigned his frontier post because his mother was old, an imperial edict in the emperor's own hand was issued, saying: 'You have pacified and comforted the region for years; your reputation and achievements are both outstanding; in securing the frontier and calming the borders you truly fulfill the court's expectations.'
translations.idiomatic: Examination shows that when Zhi resigned his frontier post because his mother was elderly, the emperor issued a personal edict: 'You have governed this region for years with outstanding reputation and achievement; in securing the frontier you have fulfilled the court's expectations.'

sentences.zh: 及其歿也，又加顯贈，言祉誠著累朝，效彰內外，作牧岷區，字萌之績驟聞。

translations.literal: When he died, eminent posthumous honors were again added, stating that Zhi's loyalty was manifest through successive reigns, his achievements renowned within and without, that as governor of the Min region his nurturing achievements were suddenly heard of.
translations.idiomatic: At his death eminent posthumous honors were added, stating that Zhi's loyalty was manifest through successive reigns, his achievements renowned at court and on the frontier, and that as governor of the Min region his nurturing achievements were widely acclaimed.

sentences.zh: 詔冊褒美，無替倫望。

translations.literal: Edicts and patent letters praised him; his standing among peers was unimpaired.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial edicts praised him without diminishing his standing among peers.

sentences.zh: 然君子使人器之義，無求備德。

translations.literal: Yet the gentleman uses men for their capacities and does not demand complete virtue.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the gentleman employs men for their capacities and does not demand perfection in every virtue.

sentences.zh: 有數德優劣不同，剛而能克，亦為德焉。

translations.literal: When several virtues differ in quality, firmness that can overcome is also a virtue.
translations.idiomatic: When virtues differ in quality, firmness that can overcome obstacles is itself a virtue.

sentences.zh: 謹依諡法，布德行剛曰『景』，謂前議為允。」

translations.literal: According to the posthumous-title law, 'displaying virtue with a firm disposition' is Jing; we hold the earlier proposal to be fitting."
translations.idiomatic: According to the law of posthumous titles, 'displaying virtue with firm resolve' is Jing; we hold the earlier proposal to be fitting."

sentences.zh: 司徒右長史張烈、主簿李瑒刺稱：「案祉歷宦累朝，當官之稱。

translations.literal: Right Chief Clerk Zhang Lie and Registrar Li Chang of the Minister of Education submitted: "Investigation shows that Zhi served through successive reigns with a reputation fitting to his office.
translations.idiomatic: Right Chief Clerk Zhang Lie and Registrar Li Chang of the Minister of Education submitted: "Investigation shows that Zhi served through successive reigns with a reputation fitting to his office.

sentences.zh: 委捍西南，邊隅靖遏。

translations.literal: Entrusted with defending the southwest, he brought peace and restraint to the frontier corners.
translations.idiomatic: Entrusted with defending the southwest, he brought peace to the frontier.

sentences.zh: 準行易名，奬誡攸在。

translations.literal: In fixing conduct and changing the name lies the purpose of reward and admonition.
translations.idiomatic: In fixing conduct and bestowing a posthumous name lies the purpose of reward and admonition.

sentences.zh: 竊謂無虧體例。」

translations.literal: We consider that this does not impair precedent."
translations.idiomatic: We consider that this does not impair precedent."

sentences.zh: 尚書李韶又述奏以府寺為允，靈太后可其奏。

translations.literal: Director of the Secretariat Li Shao again submitted that the ministry and temple offices were in agreement; Empress Dowager Ling approved the memorial.
translations.idiomatic: Director of the Secretariat Li Shao again submitted that the ministry and temple offices were in agreement; Empress Dowager Ling approved the memorial.

sentences.zh: 祉自當官，不憚強禦，朝廷以為剛斷，時有檢覆，每令出使。

translations.literal: From the time Zhi held office he did not fear the powerful; the court regarded him as firm and decisive, and when inspections were needed he was often sent on missions.
translations.idiomatic: Throughout his career Zhi did not fear the powerful; the court regarded him as firm and decisive, and when inspections were needed he was often dispatched on missions.

sentences.zh: 好慕名利，頗為深文，所經之處，人號天狗下。

translations.literal: He loved and coveted fame and profit, was rather given to harsh legal constructions, and wherever he went people called it 'the celestial dog descending.'
translations.idiomatic: He coveted fame and profit, was given to harsh legal constructions, and wherever he went people said 'the celestial dog has descended.'

sentences.zh: 及出將臨州，並無恩潤，兵民患其嚴虐焉。

translations.literal: When he went out as a general or took up a governorship there was no kindness or generosity; soldiers and people alike suffered under his severity and cruelty.
translations.idiomatic: When he served as general or governor he showed no kindness; soldiers and civilians alike suffered under his severity.

sentences.zh: 崔暹，字元欽，本云清河東武城人也。

translations.literal: Cui Xian, courtesy name Yuanqin, was originally said to be a man of Dongwucheng in Qinghe.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Xian, courtesy name Yuanqin, was said to be a native of Dongwucheng in Qinghe.

sentences.zh: 世家于滎陽、潁川之間。

translations.literal: His clan had long been established between Xingyang and Yingchuan.
translations.idiomatic: His family had long been established between Xingyang and Yingchuan.

sentences.zh: 性猛酷，少仁恕，姦猾好利，能事勢家。

translations.literal: His nature was fierce and cruel, with little humanity or forbearance; he was cunning, greedy, and skilled at serving powerful families.
translations.idiomatic: He was fierce and cruel, lacking humanity or forbearance; cunning and greedy, he excelled at currying favor with the powerful.

sentences.zh: 初以秀才累遷南兗州刺史，盜用官瓦，贓污狼藉，為御史中尉李平所糾，免官。

translations.literal: At first, through the xiucai examination he rose step by step to Governor of Southern Yanzhou; he misappropriated official roof tiles, his corruption was flagrant, and he was impeached and dismissed by Director of the Imperial Secretariat Li Ping.
translations.idiomatic: Having entered office through the xiucai examination, he rose to Governor of Southern Yanzhou; he misappropriated official roof tiles, his corruption was flagrant, and Director Li Ping impeached and dismissed him.

sentences.zh: 後行豫州事，尋即真。

translations.literal: Later he acted as administrator of Yuzhou and soon received the full appointment.
translations.idiomatic: He later served as acting administrator of Yuzhou and soon received the full appointment.

sentences.zh: 坐遣子析戶，分隸三縣，廣占田宅，藏匿官奴，障吝陂葦，侵盜公私，為御史中尉王顯所彈，免官。

translations.literal: He was charged with sending his son to divide the household and register members in three counties, extensively seizing fields and residences, concealing government slaves, monopolizing pond reeds, and plundering public and private property; Director Wang Xian impeached him and he was dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: He was charged with having his son divide the household across three counties, seizing vast tracts of land, concealing government slaves, monopolizing pond reeds, and plundering public and private property; Director Wang Xian impeached him and he was dismissed.

sentences.zh: 後累遷平北將軍、瀛州刺史。

translations.literal: Later he was promoted step by step to General Who Pacifies the North and Governor of Yingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was later promoted to General Who Pacifies the North and Governor of Yingzhou.

sentences.zh: 貪暴安忍，民庶患之。

translations.literal: He was greedy, violent, and calmly ruthless; the people suffered from him.
translations.idiomatic: Greedy, violent, and pitiless, he was a scourge to the populace.

sentences.zh: 嘗出獵州北，單騎至於民村。

translations.literal: Once when hunting north of the province he rode alone to a commoners' village.
translations.idiomatic: Once while hunting north of the province he rode alone into a village.

sentences.zh: 井有汲水婦人，暹令飲馬，因問曰：「崔瀛州何如？」

translations.literal: At a well was a woman drawing water; Xian had his horse drink and then asked: "What of Cui, Governor of Yingzhou?"
translations.idiomatic: At a well a woman was drawing water; Xian had his horse drink and asked: "What do you think of Governor Cui of Yingzhou?"

sentences.zh: 婦人不知其暹也，答曰：「百姓何罪，得如此癩兒刺史！」

translations.literal: The woman did not know it was Xian and answered: "What crime have the common people committed, to get such a leprous wretch for governor!"
translations.idiomatic: The woman did not recognize him and replied: "What crime have we committed, to get such a leprous wretch for governor!"

sentences.zh: 暹默然而去。

translations.literal: Xian departed in silence.
translations.idiomatic: Xian departed in silence.

sentences.zh: 以不稱職被解還京。

translations.literal: For incompetence he was dismissed and returned to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Deemed unfit for office, he was dismissed and recalled to the capital.

sentences.zh: 武川鎮反，詔暹為都督，隸大都督李崇討之。

translations.literal: When Wuchuan garrison rebelled, an edict appointed Xian as Commander, subordinate to Grand Commander Li Chong to campaign against them.
translations.idiomatic: When Wuchuan garrison rebelled, Xian was appointed Commander under Grand Commander Li Chong to suppress the revolt.

sentences.zh: 違崇節度，為賊所敗，單騎潛還。

translations.literal: He violated Chong's commands, was defeated by the rebels, and slipped back alone on horseback.
translations.idiomatic: He disobeyed Chong's orders, was defeated by the rebels, and fled back alone.

sentences.zh: 禁於廷尉。

translations.literal: He was imprisoned by the Court of Judicial Review.
translations.idiomatic: He was imprisoned by the Court of Judicial Review.

sentences.zh: 以女妓園田貨元叉，獲免。

translations.literal: He bribed Yuan Cha with female entertainers, gardens, and fields, and obtained release.
translations.idiomatic: He bribed Yuan Cha with female entertainers, gardens, and fields and obtained his release.

sentences.zh: 建義初遇害於河陰。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Jianyi era he was killed at Heyin.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Jianyi era he was killed at Heyin.

sentences.zh: 贈司徒公、冀州刺史，追封武津縣公。

translations.literal: He was posthumously granted Duke of the Secretariat and Governor of Jizhou, and enfeoffed as Duke of Wujin County.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously granted the title Duke of the Secretariat and Governor of Jizhou, and enfeoffed as Duke of Wujin County.

sentences.zh: 子瓚，字紹珍。

translations.literal: His son Zan, courtesy name Shaozhen.
translations.idiomatic: His son Zan, courtesy name Shaozhen.

sentences.zh: 位兼尚書左丞，卒。

translations.literal: He held the concurrent post of Left Vice Director of the Secretariat and died in office.
translations.idiomatic: He served concurrently as Left Vice Director of the Secretariat and died in office.

sentences.zh: 瓚妻，莊帝妹也，後封襄城長公主，故特贈瓚冀州刺史。

translations.literal: Zan's wife was a sister of Emperor Zhuang; later she was enfeoffed as Princess Chang of Xiangcheng, and therefore Zan was specially posthumously granted Governor of Jizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Zan's wife was a sister of Emperor Zhuang; she was later enfeoffed as Princess Chang of Xiangcheng, and Zan was therefore posthumously granted the title Governor of Jizhou.

sentences.zh: 子茂，字祖昂，襲祖爵。

translations.literal: His son Mao, courtesy name Zu'ang, inherited his grandfather's title.
translations.idiomatic: His son Mao, courtesy name Zu'ang, inherited his grandfather's title.

sentences.zh: 酈道元，字善長，范陽人也。

translations.literal: Li Daoyuan, courtesy name Shanchang, was a man of Fanyang.
translations.idiomatic: Li Daoyuan, courtesy name Shanchang, was a native of Fanyang.

sentences.zh: 青州刺史範之子。

translations.literal: He was the son of Fan, Governor of Qingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was the son of Fan, Governor of Qingzhou.

sentences.zh: 太和中，為尚書主客郎。

translations.literal: In the Taihe era he served as Master of Guests in the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: During the Taihe era he served as Master of Guests in the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 御史中尉李彪以道元秉法清勤，引為治書侍御史。

translations.literal: Director of the Imperial Secretariat Li Biao, because Daoyuan upheld the law with integrity and diligence, recommended him as Attendant Imperial Censor for Legal Documents.
translations.idiomatic: Director Li Biao, recognizing Daoyuan's integrity and diligence in upholding the law, recommended him as Attendant Imperial Censor for Legal Documents.

sentences.zh: 累遷輔國將軍、東荊州刺史。

translations.literal: He rose step by step to General Who Supports the State and Governor of Eastern Jingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to General Who Supports the State and Governor of Eastern Jingzhou.

sentences.zh: 威猛為治，蠻民詣闕訟其刻峻，坐免官。

translations.literal: He governed with ferocity and severity; barbarian peoples went to the palace to sue him for harshness and he was dismissed from office.
translations.idiomatic: He governed with ferocity; tribal peoples petitioned the throne accusing him of harshness, and he was dismissed.

sentences.zh: 久之，行河南尹，尋即真。

translations.literal: After a long while he acted as Intendant of Henan and soon received the full appointment.
translations.idiomatic: After some time he served as acting Intendant of Henan and soon received the full appointment.

sentences.zh: 肅宗以沃野、懷朔、薄骨律、武川、撫冥、柔玄、懷荒、禦夷諸鎮並改為州，其郡縣戍名令準古城邑。

translations.literal: Emperor Suzong converted the garrisons of Woye, Huaishuo, Bogulü, Wuchuan, Fuming, Rouxuan, Huaihuang, and Yuyi into prefectures, ordering that their commandery, county, and garrison names follow ancient cities and towns.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Suzong converted the garrisons of Woye, Huaishuo, Bogulü, Wuchuan, Fuming, Rouxuan, Huaihuang, and Yuyi into prefectures, ordering that their administrative names follow ancient place-names.

sentences.zh: 詔道元持節兼黃門侍郎，與都督李崇籌宜置立，裁減去留，儲兵積粟，以為邊備。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Daoyuan, bearing the staff of authority and concurrently Attendant Gentleman of the Yellow Gate, together with Commander Li Chong to plan appropriate establishments, reduce or retain posts, store troops and accumulate grain, and thereby prepare frontier defenses.
translations.idiomatic: An edict appointed Daoyuan, bearing the staff of authority and concurrently Attendant Gentleman of the Yellow Gate, together with Commander Li Chong to plan the new arrangements, reduce redundant posts, stockpile troops and grain, and strengthen frontier defenses.

sentences.zh: 未幾，除安南將軍、御史中尉。

translations.literal: Before long he was appointed General Who Pacifies the South and Director of the Imperial Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was appointed General Who Pacifies the South and Director of the Imperial Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 道元素有嚴猛之稱。

translations.literal: Daoyuan had long borne a reputation for severity and fierceness.
translations.idiomatic: Daoyuan had long borne a reputation for severity and fierceness.

sentences.zh: 司州牧、汝南王悅嬖近左右丘念，常與臥起。

translations.literal: The Governor of Sizhou, Prince of Runan Yue, favored his attendant Qiu Nian and often slept and rose with him.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Yue of Runan, Governor of Sizhou, favored his attendant Qiu Nian and often shared his bed.

sentences.zh: 及選州官，多由於念。

translations.literal: When selecting provincial officials, most appointments went through Nian.
translations.idiomatic: Most provincial appointments went through Nian.

sentences.zh: 念匿於悅第，時還其家，道元收念付獄。

translations.literal: Nian hid in Yue's residence and sometimes returned to his own home; Daoyuan seized Nian and handed him over to prison.
translations.idiomatic: Nian hid in Yue's residence, occasionally returning home; Daoyuan arrested him and sent him to prison.

sentences.zh: 悅啟靈太后請全之，敕赦之。

translations.literal: Yue petitioned Empress Dowager Ling to spare him; an edict ordered his release.
translations.idiomatic: Yue petitioned Empress Dowager Ling to spare him; an edict ordered his release.

sentences.zh: 道元遂盡其命，因以劾悅。

translations.literal: Daoyuan thereupon took his life, and thereby impeached Yue.
translations.idiomatic: Daoyuan executed him and impeached Yue.

sentences.zh: 是時雍州刺史蕭寶夤反狀稍露，悅等諷朝廷遣為關右大使，遂為寶夤所害，死於陰盤驛亭。

translations.literal: At that time Xiao Baoyin, Governor of Yongzhou, showed signs of rebellion; Yue and others insinuated to the court that Daoyuan be sent as envoy to the Guanxi region, and he was thereupon killed by Baoyin at the Yinyan post station.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Xiao Baoyin, Governor of Yongzhou, showed signs of rebellion; Yue and others persuaded the court to send Daoyuan as envoy to the Guanxi region, where Baoyin killed him at the Yinyan post station.

sentences.zh: 道元好學，歷覽奇書。

translations.literal: Daoyuan loved learning and read widely in rare books.
translations.idiomatic: Daoyuan loved learning and read widely in rare books.

sentences.zh: 撰注水經四十卷、本志十三篇，又為七聘及諸文，皆行於世。

translations.literal: He compiled a commentary to the Water Classic in forty juan and thirteen chapters of local records, and also wrote the Seven Embassies and other works, all of which circulated in his time.
translations.idiomatic: He compiled a forty-juan commentary to the Water Classic, thirteen chapters of local records, the Seven Embassies, and other works, all of which circulated widely.

sentences.zh: 然兄弟不能篤穆，又多嫌忌，時論薄之。

translations.literal: Yet the brothers could not maintain harmony and were much given to suspicion; contemporary opinion looked down on them.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the brothers could not maintain harmony and were much given to suspicion; contemporary opinion looked down on them.

sentences.zh: 谷楷，昌黎人，濮陽公渾曾孫。

translations.literal: Gu Kai was a man of Changli, great-grandson of Hun, Duke of Puyang.
translations.idiomatic: Gu Kai was a native of Changli and great-grandson of Hun, Duke of Puyang.

sentences.zh: 稍遷奉車都尉。

translations.literal: He was gradually promoted to Commandant of the Imperial Carriages.
translations.idiomatic: He was gradually promoted to Commandant of the Imperial Carriages.

sentences.zh: 時沙門法慶反於冀州，雖大軍討破，而妖帥尚未梟除。

translations.literal: At that time the monk Faqing rebelled in Jizhou; though the great army defeated him, the demonic chieftains had not yet all been executed.
