translations.idiomatic: At that time the monk Faqing rebelled in Jizhou; though the imperial army defeated him, the rebel leaders had not yet all been captured and executed.

sentences.zh: 詔楷詣冀州追捕，皆擒獲之。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Kai to go to Jizhou to pursue and capture them; he seized them all.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered Kai to Jizhou to hunt them down; he captured them all.

sentences.zh: 楷眇一目而性甚嚴忍，前後奉使皆以酷暴為名。

translations.literal: Kai was blind in one eye and by nature very stern and ruthless; in successive missions he was known for cruelty and violence.
translations.idiomatic: Kai was blind in one eye and by nature stern and ruthless; on every mission he was known for cruelty.

sentences.zh: 時人號曰「瞎虎」。

translations.literal: People of the time called him 'the Blind Tiger.'
translations.idiomatic: People of the time called him 'the Blind Tiger.'

sentences.zh: 尋為城門校尉，卒。

translations.literal: Soon he became Commandant of the City Gates and died.
translations.idiomatic: He soon became Commandant of the City Gates and died in office.

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：士之立名，其途不一，或以循良進，或以嚴酷顯。

translations.literal: The historiographer says: In establishing a name, gentlemen have not one path alone—some advance through gentleness and goodness, others become prominent through severity and cruelty.
translations.idiomatic: The historiographer writes: Gentlemen establish their reputations by diverse paths—some rise through benevolence and integrity, others through severity and cruelty.

sentences.zh: 故寬猛相資，德刑互設，然不嚴而化，君子所先。

translations.literal: Thus leniency and severity complement one another, virtue and punishment are set up in turn, yet transformation without severity is what the gentleman prioritizes.
translations.idiomatic: Leniency and severity complement one another, virtue and punishment work in tandem, yet the gentleman prioritizes transforming people without relying on harshness.

sentences.zh: 于洛侯等為惡不同，同歸於酷。

translations.literal: Yu Luohou and the others committed different evils, yet all alike ended in cruelty.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Luohou and the others committed different crimes, yet all alike ended in cruelty.

sentences.zh: 肆其毒螫，多行殘忍。

translations.literal: They unleashed their venomous stings and frequently acted with cruelty.
translations.idiomatic: They unleashed their venom and frequently acted with cruelty.

sentences.zh: 賤人肌膚，同諸木石；

translations.literal: They debased human flesh and skin to the level of wood and stone;
translations.idiomatic: They treated human flesh no differently than wood and stone;

sentences.zh: 輕人性命，甚於芻狗。

translations.literal: they held human life cheaper than straw dogs.
translations.idiomatic: they held human life cheaper than straw dogs.

sentences.zh: 長惡不悛，鮮有不及。

translations.literal: Persisting in evil without repentance, few escaped the consequences.
translations.idiomatic: Persisting in evil without repentance, few escaped the consequences.

sentences.zh: 故或身嬰罪戮，或憂恚顛隕。

translations.literal: Therefore some personally suffered punishment and execution, others were consumed by grief and distress and perished.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore some suffered execution, others were consumed by grief and perished.

sentences.zh: 異途皆斃，各其宜焉。

translations.literal: By different paths they all met destruction—each received what was fitting.
translations.idiomatic: By different paths they all met destruction—each received what was fitting.

sentences.zh: 凡百君子，以為有天道矣。

translations.literal: All gentlemen considered that the Way of Heaven was at work.
translations.idiomatic: All gentlemen considered that the Way of Heaven was at work.

sentences.zh: 校勘記

translations.literal: Collation Notes
translations.idiomatic: Collation Notes

sentences.zh: 魏書卷八十九 諸本目錄注「闕」，但卷後無宋人校語。

translations.literal: In the table of contents of various editions of the Book of Wei, juan 89 is marked 'deficient,' yet there are no Song-dynasty collation notes at the end of the scroll.
translations.idiomatic: In the table of contents of various editions of the Book of Wei, juan 89 is marked 'deficient,' yet there are no Song-dynasty collation notes at the end of the scroll.

sentences.zh: 殿本考證云「魏收書亡，後人所補」，乃據目錄而言。

translations.literal: The Palatial Edition textual verification states that 'Wei Shou's original text is lost and later persons supplemented it'—this judgment is based on the table of contents.
translations.idiomatic: The Palatial Edition textual verification states that 'Wei Shou's original text is lost and was supplemented by later hands'—a judgment based on the table of contents.

sentences.zh: 今按傳序與北史卷八七酷吏傳序不同，諸傳也多出入。

translations.literal: Now examining the matter, the preface to the biographies differs from the preface to the Cruel Officials biographies in juan 87 of the History of the Northern Dynasties, and the individual biographies also diverge in many places.
translations.idiomatic: Examination shows that the preface differs from that in juan 87 of the History of the Northern Dynasties, and the individual biographies diverge in many places.

sentences.zh: 北史高遵傳

translations.literal: The biography of Gao Zun in the History of the Northern Dynasties
translations.idiomatic: The biography of Gao Zun in the History of the Northern Dynasties

sentences.zh: 〈附卷三一高允傳〉、

translations.literal: 〈attached to the biography of Gao Yun, juan 31〉
translations.idiomatic: 〈attached to the biography of Gao Yun, juan 31〉

sentences.zh: 酈道元傳

translations.literal: and the biography of Li Daoyuan
translations.idiomatic: and the biography of Li Daoyuan

sentences.zh: 〈附卷二七酈範傳〉

translations.literal: 〈attached to the biography of Li Fan, juan 27〉
translations.idiomatic: 〈attached to the biography of Li Fan, juan 27〉

sentences.zh: 均詳於此傳，谷楷傳則北史略去殺變亂人眾事。

translations.literal: are all given in detail in this biography; the biography of Gu Kai in the Northern History omits the matter of killing and disturbing the populace.
translations.idiomatic: are all given in detail here; the Northern History biography of Gu Kai omits his killings and disturbances among the populace.

sentences.zh: 此卷非以北史補甚明。

translations.literal: It is quite clear that this scroll was not supplemented from the Northern History.
translations.idiomatic: It is quite clear that this scroll was not supplemented from the Northern History.

sentences.zh: 但序甚簡短，高、酈二傳敍事較北史簡略。

translations.literal: Yet the preface is very brief, and the narratives of the Gao and Li biographies are more concise than those in the Northern History.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the preface is very brief, and the Gao and Li biographies are more concise than those in the Northern History.

sentences.zh: 傳論全同北史，而北史實本隋書卷七四酷吏傳論，不過稍加改易而已，魏收豈能用隋書語，知是此傳襲取北史。

translations.literal: The biographical judgment is entirely identical to the Northern History, yet the Northern History in fact derives from the judgment on Cruel Officials in juan 74 of the Book of Sui, with only slight alterations. How could Wei Shou have used language from the Sui book? It is known that this biography borrowed from the Northern History.
translations.idiomatic: The biographical judgment is identical to the Northern History, which in turn derives from juan 74 of the Book of Sui with only slight alterations. Wei Shou could not have used Sui-dynasty language; this judgment was borrowed from the Northern History.

sentences.zh: 則此卷必非魏書原文，當是以高氏小史等書補，傳末校語偶脫。

translations.literal: Thus this scroll cannot be the original text of the Book of Wei; it must have been supplemented from works such as the Brief History of the Gao Clan, and the collation note at the end of the biography was accidentally lost.
translations.idiomatic: Thus this scroll cannot be Wei Shou's original text; it was likely supplemented from works such as the Brief History of the Gao Clan, and the collation note at the end was accidentally lost.

sentences.zh: 遂領逃連及諸畜牧者 張森楷云：「『逃連』字不可解，疑有誤。」

translations.literal: then led the taolian and various herdsmen. Zhang Senkai says: "The characters 'taolian' are incomprehensible; there is probably an error."
translations.idiomatic: He then led the taolian and various herdsmen. Zhang Senkai notes: "The characters 'taolian' are incomprehensible; the text is probably corrupt."

sentences.zh: 今臺使心協前事 北史卷八七張赦提傳「心協」作「止挾」。

translations.literal: Now the imperial envoy xinxie the earlier matter. In the biography of Zhang Sheti in juan 87 of the History of the Northern Dynasties, 'xinxie' is written as 'zhi xie.'
translations.idiomatic: Now the imperial envoy xinxie the earlier matter. In Zhang Sheti's biography in juan 87 of the History of the Northern Dynasties, 'xinxie' reads 'zhi xie' (harbored resentment and exploited).

sentences.zh: 按「協」謂威脅，與文義不叶，疑作「挾」是。

translations.literal: Commentary: 'xie' means to threaten by force, which does not fit the sense of the passage; 'xie' (to harbor and exploit) is probably correct.
translations.idiomatic: Commentary: 'xie' as 'threaten' does not fit the context; 'xie' (harbor resentment and exploit) is probably correct.

sentences.zh: 為司空令輔國長史 按司空屬官無令。

translations.literal: served as Chief Aide to the Support-the-State Army under the Minister of Works. Commentary: Among the subordinates of the Minister of Works there is no office of 'ling.'
translations.idiomatic: He served as Chief Aide to the Support-the-State Army under the Minister of Works. Commentary: The Minister of Works had no office titled 'ling.'

sentences.zh: 「令」字疑衍，意謂以輔國將軍為司空長史。

translations.literal: The character 'ling' is probably a superfluous addition; the meaning is that he served as Chief Clerk of the Secretariat to the Minister of Works with the rank of General Who Supports the State.
translations.idiomatic: The character 'ling' is probably a scribal error; the meaning is that he served as Chief Clerk to the Minister of Works with the rank of General Who Supports the State.

sentences.zh: 但亦晦澀，或有訛脫。

translations.literal: Yet this is also obscure and difficult; there may be corruption or omission.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the passage remains obscure; there may be corruption or omission.

sentences.zh: 或憂恚顛隕 諸本「顛」作「值」，北史卷八七作「俱」，隋書卷七四酷吏傳論作「顛」。

translations.literal: or were consumed by grief and distress and perished. In various editions 'dian' is written as 'zhi'; juan 87 of the Northern History has 'ju'; the judgment on Cruel Officials in juan 74 of the Book of Sui has 'dian.'
translations.idiomatic: Or they were consumed by grief and perished. Various editions read 'dian' as 'zhi'; juan 87 of the Northern History has 'ju'; juan 74 of the Book of Sui has 'dian.'

sentences.zh: 按「值」字顯訛，「俱」字雖可通，然「顛隕」與上句「罪戮」對文，今據隋書改。

translations.literal: Commentary: The character 'zhi' is clearly erroneous; 'ju' can be made to fit, yet 'dian yun' (to topple and perish) forms a parallel with 'zui lu' (punishment and execution) in the preceding clause; the text is emended according to the Book of Sui.
translations.idiomatic: Commentary: 'zhi' is clearly erroneous; though 'ju' can be construed, 'dian yun' (to topple and perish) parallels 'zui lu' (punishment and execution) in the preceding clause; the text is emended according to the Book of Sui.
